title: Best Ebac Dehumidifier (2026): Neptune, CD30-S, WM80-D, AD850E
dek: Britain's best-known dehumidifier maker sells a very different lineup in the U.S. — all heavy-duty, all built for crawl spaces, restoration and wall-mount installs.
description: The best Ebac dehumidifier for U.S. buyers: the Neptune, CD30-S, WM80-D and AD850E compared, plus why Ebac's UK home models aren't sold here.
intro: Ebac is a British manufacturer with deep roots in the category: founded in 1973 in Newton Aycliffe, England, it built the UK's first mass-produced home dehumidifier in 1980. But if you search for an **Ebac dehumidifier** in the U.S. expecting a reasonably priced bedroom unit, you'll be surprised. The lineup sold here is entirely restoration, marine and commercial-grade equipment, and every model costs four figures.

That's not a reason to skip the brand. It just means an Ebac makes sense for specific jobs: a cold crawl space, a boat, a flood dry-out, or a basement where you want the dehumidifier mounted on the wall and off the floor for good. We compared the four Ebac models you can actually buy in the U.S. and flagged when a cheaper alternative is the smarter call.
topPicksLead: The **Ebac Neptune** is the best all-around Ebac for most U.S. buyers: a portable, 52-pint restoration-grade unit that's rated to work down to 33°F.

products.name: Ebac Neptune Portable Dehumidifier
products.whyWeLoveIt: It's the closest thing to a general-purpose pick in Ebac's U.S. range: strong enough for an active drying job and portable enough for one person to move between rooms or job sites.
products.performance: Ebac rates it at 52 pints a day under AHAM conditions (80°F, 60% RH) with 282 CFM of airflow. A rotary compressor with hot-gas defrost keeps it working down to 33°F, and it runs on standard 115V power with a 25-foot cord, so most homes won't need a dedicated circuit.

products.name: Ebac CD30-S Low-Temperature Dehumidifier
products.award: Best for crawl spaces and boats
pros: Heavy-duty steel housing for marine use
products.whyWeLoveIt: This is the Ebac to buy when the real problem is cold, not capacity. Many household units ice up in the 40s; the CD30-S keeps working in unheated crawl spaces and boat holds.
products.performance: It removes up to 24 pints a day at 170 CFM and is sized for roughly 3,000 cubic feet. It can be wall- or bracket-mounted to stay out of low-clearance spaces, and a pump-equipped sibling, the CD30-SE, is also available. If 33°F operation isn't a must, our [crawl space dehumidifier guide](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) has less expensive options.

products.name: Ebac WM80-D Wall-Mounted Dehumidifier
pros: Built-in condensate pump with 25 ft drain tube
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a basement or utility room you want free of floor-standing equipment permanently, the WM80-D hangs on the wall and pumps its own water away. It's a set-and-forget solution rather than a drying-job tool.
products.performance: It's rated at roughly 56–62 pints a day, depending on the source and test conditions, across about 1,500 square feet. The low current draw is friendlier to older electrical panels. Compare other options in our [wall-mounted dehumidifier guide](/best/best-wall-mounted-dehumidifier/).

products.name: Ebac AD850E Wall-Mounted Dehumidifier
pros: 95 pints/day — largest in Ebac's U.S. lineup
cons: Priciest Ebac sold in the U.S.
products.whyWeLoveIt: When a full basement, large storage area or facility has outgrown the WM80-D, the AD850E delivers far more capacity in the same off-the-floor format.
products.performance: It removes up to 95 pints a day at 294 CFM with a draw of about 7 amps, and it's rated for continuous operation. For even larger industrial spaces, see the bigger Ebac units in our [warehouse dehumidifier guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-warehouse/).

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compared Ebac's published capacity, airflow, operating-temperature and electrical specs, checked which models are genuinely available to U.S. buyers, and set them against AlorAir, Santa Fe and other commercial-grade rivals. We searched the CPSC recall database and read reviews from contractors, boat owners and homeowners.
Because every U.S. Ebac is expensive, we weighed one question above all: does this job actually need commercial-grade equipment? Where it doesn't, we say so.

sections.heading: What to look for in an Ebac dehumidifier

items.label: A real need for commercial grade
items.text: If a household unit would handle your space, an Ebac isn't the economical choice. Start with our [best dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier/) picks.

items.label: Low-temperature operation
items.text: The CD30-S and Neptune's 33°F ratings are the reason to choose them for unheated crawl spaces, garages and boats.

items.label: Wall mounting
items.text: The WM80-D and AD850E free up floor space entirely — worth it in a basement used for storage or work.

items.label: Capacity matched to the space
items.text: 24 pints for a crawl space, 52 for a portable drying job, 95 for a full basement or facility.

items.label: LGR if you're drying a flood
items.text: Ebac's units use standard refrigerant designs. For active water-damage dry-outs, purpose-built LGR machines are stronger; see our [commercial dehumidifier guide](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: Why every U.S. Ebac dehumidifier costs four figures

blocks.text: In the UK, Ebac is known for affordable home units such as the 2650e, 3650e and 3850e — machines that compete with mainstream room dehumidifiers on price. None of those domestic models are sold through U.S. retailers. What's available here is Ebac's restoration, marine and commercial hardware, the same family as its larger industrial units.

blocks.title: Looking for the Ebac 3650e?
blocks.text: The 3650e is a UK-market home model built for 230V power and isn't sold in the U.S. For a comparable household unit here, look at mainstream brands in our [dehumidifier brands guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) — they cost a fraction of any U.S. Ebac.

Both build tough, professional-grade machines. AlorAir's Storm line is purpose-built LGR equipment optimized for pulling water out of air that's already fairly dry — the hardest phase of a flood dry-out — while Ebac's strengths are low-temperature operation, wall-mount formats and rugged steel housings. Compare the AlorAir range in our [AlorAir dehumidifier guide](/best/best-alorair-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: Which Ebac dehumidifier should you buy?

items: **You're drying out a wet room or job site and want one portable machine:** the Neptune. Its 52 pints a day and 33°F rating cover most restoration-style work, and one person can move it.
**Your crawl space or boat sits near freezing for months:** the CD30-S. It gives up capacity for cold-weather reliability and a footprint that fits low-clearance spaces.
**You want a permanent, out-of-the-way basement solution:** the WM80-D. It hangs on the wall, pumps its own water and leaves the floor free.
**The space is a full basement, archive or commercial storeroom:** the AD850E, which nearly doubles the WM80-D's rated capacity.
**It's an ordinary damp bedroom or living room:** none of them. A household 20- to 50-pint unit will do the job for far less money.

blocks.text: Whichever you choose, plan the drainage before it arrives. The wall-mount models pump through a tube to a drain or outside wall, and portable units work best with a hose to a floor drain so they never stall with a full tank. Our [where to place a dehumidifier](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) guide covers spacing and airflow.

The **Ebac Neptune** is the best all-around Ebac for restoration and heavy-moisture work. Choose the **CD30-S** for cold crawl spaces and boats, the **WM80-D** to keep a basement floor clear, and the **AD850E** for the largest spaces. Just go in knowing every U.S. Ebac is commercial-grade equipment at commercial-grade prices; for a typical damp room, a mainstream household unit is the better value.

faqs.q: What is the best Ebac dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For most U.S. buyers, the Ebac Neptune: a portable, 52-pint-a-day (AHAM) unit with 282 CFM airflow and low-temperature operation down to 33°F. For crawl spaces, the CD30-S; for wall-mount basement installs, the WM80-D or the larger AD850E.

faqs.q: Is Ebac a good dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: Yes, for the market it serves. Ebac has built dehumidifiers since the 1970s and is one of Britain's best-known makers. In the U.S., though, it sells only restoration and commercial-grade models, not budget room units.

faqs.q: Why are Ebac dehumidifiers so expensive in the U.S.?
faqs.a: Because the models sold here are heavy-duty units for crawl spaces, contractors and marine use. Ebac's affordable UK home models, such as the 2650e, 3650e and 3850e, aren't sold in the U.S.

faqs.q: Does Ebac make a crawl space dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Yes. The CD30-S (and the pump-equipped CD30-SE) is built for crawl spaces and boats. It runs down to 33°F, removes up to 24 pints a day and can be bracket-mounted in low-clearance spaces.

It's Ebac's largest U.S. model: a wall-mounted unit rated at up to 95 pints a day with 294 CFM airflow, a built-in pump and a design meant for continuous, round-the-clock operation in full basements and commercial storage spaces.

faqs.q: How does Ebac compare to AlorAir?
faqs.a: AlorAir's Storm LGR line is purpose-built for drying out floods quickly. Ebac's Neptune and AD850E are strong standard-refrigerant units with excellent cold-weather and wall-mount options, at similar or higher prices.

faqs.q: Can an Ebac dehumidifier run in a cold garage or crawl space?
faqs.a: The Neptune and CD30-S are both rated to operate down to 33°F, which is colder than most household dehumidifiers can manage without icing up. That makes them good fits for unheated garages, crawl spaces and boats.
